A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LODGE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction-quality and rendering-speed experiments, component ablations, and mobile-device measurements in Section 4, Tables 1–4, and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds CityGS comparison results and a qualitative observation about blending artifacts.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and A.2 retain the same LOD construction, smoothing, pruning, threshold selection, position-based clustering, visibility filtering, and two-chunk opacity blending. Added explanations of chunk contents and loading do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SmallCity, Campus, Alameda, London, and NYC. v2 additionally reports observing no blending artifacts on Mip-NeRF 360 in Section 4. This expands reported coverage, but only through a brief qualitative statement without scene-level results.

E2.justification: v2 adds CityGS (CityGaussian) as an evaluated comparator in both Tables 1 and 2, covering all five retained scenes. It was cited but not included in these comparisons in v1. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The documented splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, and timing procedures in Section 4 and Appendices A.2–A.4 are retained. No distinct protocol is specified for the added qualitative observation. The new explanation of Gaussian count justifies an existing memory proxy.

E4.justification: Section 4 adds a brief qualitative robustness assessment of two-chunk blending when camera paths can encounter three or more chunks, reporting no observed artifacts across three datasets. No controlled new robustness experiment is documented; the quantitative ablations in Table 3 and Figure 7 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 retains seven timing measurements per test image and median aggregation. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises Zip-NeRF's PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS from 24.78/0.770/0.381 to 26.30/0.785/0.368 on SmallCity and from 21.34/0.768/0.422 to 22.04/0.781/0.416 on Campus, without explaining the revisions. Tables 1–2 add CityGS results, and Section 4 adds the no-artifact observation including Mip-NeRF 360. LODGE's numerical results and Tables 3–4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), the smoothing argument, and the greedy threshold-selection rationale are retained. Clarified variable descriptions and new informal blending hypotheses do not introduce or revise formal mathematics or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about LOD construction, automatic thresholds, chunk caching, smooth transitions, and efficient high-quality rendering on constrained devices.

C2.justification: v2 adds rationales for excluding orientation from chunk definitions, using Gaussian count as a memory proxy, and expecting two-chunk blending to suffice. It also changes the Campus explanation from Octree-GS's exposure robustness to LODGE being exposure-robust but perceptually weaker, conflicting with LODGE's better SSIM/LPIPS in Table 1. The final streaming limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly details the GPU loading sequence: retain the closest chunk, remove the previous chunk, and load the next chunk after passing a chunk center, including delayed-loading behavior. Appendix hyperparameters, hardware, processing instructions, and access links are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Mip-NeRF 360, LOD-GS, and PRoGS. CityGaussian was already cited in v1. The broader positioning relative to existing LOD, compression, and large-scene reconstruction methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds localized explanatory paragraphs about chunks, loading, visibility, and blending, revises some evaluation prose, and updates affiliations and the conference header. The main section sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain CityGS rows and adjusted ranking highlights. Figures and tables are rearranged: Figure 5 separates from Table 1, Table 2 appears below Figure 6, and Table 3 shares a page with Figure 7. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Evaluating the previously unevaluated CityGS comparator and clarifying chunk contents and GPU loading provide modest gains in comparative evidence and reproducibility. These benefits are partly offset by the newly inconsistent Campus interpretation and Figure 1 retaining its old Zip-NeRF point after Table 1 changes. The added Mip-NeRF 360 observation also lacks detailed supporting evidence.
